description:
Redwood Inference is standardizing how it represents, computes, and serves inference cost information so that Redwood Console (dashboards/observability) and Redwood Optimize (batching/caching/quantization recommendations) can rely on a single, versioned cost model spec and API. Today, cost numbers and “what counts” (prefill vs decode, cache hits, batch efficiency, quantization effects, overhead allocation, etc.) can differ across telemetry, billing hooks, and Optimize prototypes. This project defines canonical inputs/outputs for a “standard cost model” and exposes them through a stable internal API that Console and Optimize can call consistently.

Goals:
- Define a versioned cost model spec (schemas + semantics) covering model/runtime characteristics, deployment context (hosted/dedicated/private), routing/batching/caching state, and quantization profiles.
- Provide a Cost Model API (internal service + library) that returns: per-request cost estimates, aggregated cost breakdowns, and “what-if” projections for config changes (batching/caching/quantization).
- Align telemetry and billing hooks so the same primitives power: Console cost breakdown views, Optimize recommendations ROI estimates, and finance/unit-economics reporting.
- Establish governance: ownership, review process, backward compatibility rules, and deprecation policy.

Non-goals (initial phase):
- Replacing billing/RevRec systems; the API provides standardized cost primitives but does not become the billing system of record.
- Building full customer-facing pricing calculators; this is an internal API used by product surfaces.

Key stakeholders and teams:
- Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Cole Summers): API/service design, auth/tenancy, quotas/billing hooks integration.
- Telemetry & Analytics (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Caleb Johnson, Mei Lin): token-level metering inputs, aggregation, data quality.
- Console Backend & Product (Chloe Martin, Jada Williams, Felix Schneider; Marissa Cole): dashboard requirements, UX-driven fields, rollout safety.
- Optimize Product & Applied ML (Aditya Rao; Dr. Maya Srinivasan, Jonas Weber, Arjun Desai, Hassan Mirza): what-if projections, quantization/caching/batching modeling, recommendation ROI.
- Runtime Scheduling/Kernels (Sofia Ivanova, Omar El‑Sayed, Grace Kim): ensuring model inputs correctly reflect runtime realities (KV cache, batch efficiency, quant profiles).
- Finance/FP&A (Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra): alignment with unit economics, overhead allocation policy, auditability.

Phases and timeline (hypothetical, Q1 2026):
1) Discovery + requirements (2 weeks): inventory existing cost definitions, confirm Console/Optimize use-cases, define minimal v1 fields.
2) Spec + ADRs (2–3 weeks): schemas, semantics, compatibility rules; agree on performance/correctness constraints.
3) Implementation (3–4 weeks): cost-model service/library, wiring to telemetry inputs, initial endpoints, CI + conformance tests.
4) Integration + rollout (2–3 weeks): Console + Optimize adoption behind flags, validation dashboards, backtesting vs observed spend.
5) Launch + governance (ongoing): documentation, runbooks, monitoring, deprecation process.

Key deliverables:
- Confluence spec (published) + ADRs.
- Versioned schema package in the monorepo.
- Internal Cost Model API service endpoints and client.
- Console + Optimize integrations (feature flags + metrics).
- Validation harness: golden datasets, perf tests, and drift detection dashboards.

Constraints:
- Must handle high-cardinality telemetry without exploding cost/latency; API responses need bounded size.
- Must support multiple deployment modes and hardware SKUs; quantization profile modeling must be explicit and versioned.
- Must be backward-compatible for Console/Optimize and stable for finance reporting windows.

files.description: PRD for the Standard Cost Model Spec + API: user problems, Console/Optimize use-cases, success metrics, scope boundaries, phased rollout plan, and launch checklist.
Detailed design spec for Cost Model API v1: endpoints, request/response shapes, versioning, auth/tenancy, rate limits, latency targets, and failure modes.
API standards addendum for cost-model endpoints: naming, pagination/bounding rules, determinism expectations, error codes, and deprecation/versioning policy.
ADR: choose a single canonical cost model spec + API (vs per-product implementations). Includes trade-offs, ownership, and migration plan.
ADR: define cost breakdown taxonomy (prefill/decode, cache hits, batch efficiency, overhead allocation, quantization deltas) and required semantics.
Service overview: architecture diagram (text), dependencies (telemetry store, model catalog), SLA/SLOs, oncall ownership, and rollout strategy.
How-to for Console teams: client usage examples, recommended caching, pagination/bounds guidance, and testing against staging fixtures.
How-to for Optimize: calling what-if endpoints, providing workload summaries, interpreting confidence intervals, and guardrails for recommendations.
Dashboards/alerts spec: request volume, p50/p95 latency, error budgets, schema-version distribution, and drift metrics vs observed spend.
SLO doc for cost-model API: availability, latency, correctness/drift SLI definition, and escalation policy.
Runbook for incidents: common failure modes (telemetry lag, schema mismatch, cardinality blowup), mitigation steps, and rollback/feature-flag procedures.
Quantization profile cost modeling: how to parameterize quant impacts (throughput, memory, quality constraints) and map profiles into the standard cost spec.
Validation harness plan: golden datasets, replay methodology, acceptance thresholds, and how eval/perf suites validate cost-model projections.
Definition of runtime-exported inputs required by the cost model: KV cache stats, batch sizes, scheduling outcomes, and quantization execution path identifiers.
Finance-facing alignment doc: how standard cost outputs map to FP&A unit economics reporting, overhead allocation policy, and reporting windows.
Working doc capturing Optimize’s required cost fields, what-if scenarios (batching/caching/quant), and open questions for v1 vs v2.
Mock payloads and sample UI breakdown tables for Console cost views; notes on which fields are required/optional.
Early outline of schema/proto/JSON shapes, versioning approach, and notes on backwards compatibility.
Exploratory analysis of drift between observed GPU spend and token-attributed costs; hypotheses and data quality gaps.
Applied ML scratchpad for quantization ROI estimation: assumptions, constraints, and how to express uncertainty/confidence.
Console backend integration checklist, feature flag plan, and staged rollout steps across environments.
List of runtime metrics needed for cost modeling that are missing/ambiguous; owners and proposed instrumentation changes.
Performance budget worksheet: target latency, caching strategy, and cardinality constraints for cost-model computations.
PM ticket to draft and socialize PRD; includes stakeholder review checklist and acceptance criteria for v1.
Engineering ticket: create cost-model service skeleton, routing, auth, and initial endpoint scaffolding in monorepo.
Engineering ticket: define schema v1 (inputs/outputs), versioning, and codegen; includes review from Console/Optimize.
Engineering ticket: formalize telemetry inputs (token metering, cache metrics, batch stats) and data quality checks.
Engineering ticket: implement what-if cost projections for config changes (batching/caching/quantization) with guardrails.
Engineering ticket: integrate Console cost breakdown pages with the Cost Model API behind a feature flag.
Engineering ticket: wire Optimize recommendation ROI calculations to standard cost model outputs.
Engineering ticket: define drift SLI, implement monitoring pipeline, and configure alerts/dashboards.
Engineering ticket: add/standardize KV cache/batch efficiency metrics required by the cost model.
Engineering ticket: ensure model catalog exposes stable quantization profile identifiers and metadata for cost modeling.
Engineering ticket: create shared client library for internal services (Console/Optimize) with retries, timeouts, and version negotiation.
Engineering ticket: create fixture datasets and golden tests for cost computations; integrate into CI.
Engineering ticket: align quotas/billing hooks to use the same primitives; document any intentional differences.
PR adds the versioned cost-model schema package (types + docs), including initial input/output structs and serialization tests.
PR introduces internal Cost Model API endpoints (estimate + breakdown + what-if) with auth/tenancy checks and request bounds.
PR adds a shared client library with timeouts, retries, and schema version negotiation for service-to-service calls.
PR updates Console backend aggregation to call Cost Model API; includes feature flag, fallback behavior, and metrics.
PR updates Optimize ROI calculations to use standard cost outputs; includes mapping from recommendation configs to what-if inputs.
PR adds/normalizes batch efficiency and queue-time metrics to telemetry pipeline to support accurate cost inputs.
PR standardizes KV cache hit/miss metrics naming and units; updates documentation and compatibility tests.
PR adds a scheduled drift monitoring job comparing predicted vs observed costs; exports metrics for dashboards/alerts.
PR adds policy guardrails (bounds, allowed parameter ranges) for what-if scenarios to prevent expensive computations and misuse.
PR updates model catalog to expose stable quantization profile IDs + metadata used by the cost model and Optimize.
PR adds runtime-side instrumentation/export for KV cache stats and per-stage (prefill/decode) token accounting.
PR adds golden fixture datasets and deterministic tests for cost computations; integrates into CI.
PR refactors billing hooks to consume the same standardized primitives and documents any differences for invoicing.
PR adds Grafana dashboards for cost-model API latency/errors, version distribution, and drift metrics.
PR updates internal docs site with Cost Model API usage examples, field definitions, and troubleshooting notes.
Thread: cross-team discussion on cost breakdown taxonomy and what is considered ‘overhead’ vs ‘request-attributable’ cost.
Thread: platform team debate on API shape (pull vs push), request bounding, and caching strategy for Console hot paths.
Thread: applied ML + Optimize discuss how to represent quantization uncertainty and quality guardrails in what-if results.
